fatal_errors: The proposed CALPHAD-to-ML surrogate does not reconstruct the target's DFT/MTP/FEP methodology and cannot remedy inaccurate or missing CALPHAD descriptions because it merely learns their outputs.

It incorrectly treats R ln N configurational entropy as the dominant entropy of fusion. Entropy of fusion is the entropy difference between liquid and solid, so configurational contributions common to both phases can substantially cancel.
The claimed mechanism linking increasing component count, intermetallic formation, and systematic melting-point depression is not generally valid and is not established by the cited evidence.
Quantitative claims such as greater than 15% accuracy improvement, specific melting-temperature trends, and heat-capacity corrections are unsupported by the cited records.
The suggested DSC experiment is poorly matched to the stated experimental limitation for refractory alloys and does not test the target method's critical MTP-to-DFT free-energy agreement.
explanation: The response addresses the broad goal of rapidly screening refractory HEA melting properties and proposes a recognizable surrogate-model workflow, but it misses nearly every defining element of the hidden target: TaVCrW, MTP treatment of the liquid, FEP replacing thermodynamic integration, DFT reference calculations, electronic free-energy effects, solid-state short-range order, and the quantitative speed and accuracy benchmarks. Its baseline is rule-of-mixtures/CALPHAD rather than TOR-TILD with EAM potentials. The boundary conditions are generic and fail to identify dependence on MTP training quality, sub-meV/atom errors, magnetic assumptions, or GGA/LDA uncertainty. Although the falsification experiment compares several models and measurements, it cannot discriminate the target atomistic mechanism. Most supporting papers concern phase selection or general screening rather than fusion entropy, heat capacity, or validated melting free energies, so the central quantitative predictions are not evidence-backed.
